IX.|OF THE APOSTLES.|315}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, a bearded man.png|imgsize=115px|fl={{verse|chapter=9|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 22, 4. Gal. 1, 13.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Epistle vpō the Conuersion of S. Paul Ian. 25.}}∷ Saul as yet breathing forth threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of our Lord, came to the high priest, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=2}}† and asked letters of him vnto Damascus to the synagogs, that if he had found any men and vvomen of this vvay, he might bring them bound vnto Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=3}}† And as he vvent on his iourney, it chaunced that he drevv nigh to Damascus: and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1. Cor. 15, 8.''}}* sodenly a light from heauen shined round about him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=4}}† And falling on the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The heretikes that conclude CHRIST so in heauen that he can be no vvhere els til the day of Iudgement, shal hardly resolue a mã that vvould knovv vvhere CHRIST vvas vvhen he appeared here in the vvay, and spake these vvords to Saul.}}∷ Saul, Saul vvhy persecutest thou me? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=5}}† Vvho said, Vvho art thou Lord? And he, I am {{sc|Iesvs}} vvhom thou doest persecute. it is hard for thee to kicke against the pricke. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=6}}† And trembling and being astonied he said, Lord, vvhat vvilt thou haue me to doe? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=7}}† And our Lord to him, Arise, and goe into the citie, and it shal be told thee vvhat thou must doe. But the men that vvent in companie vvith him, stood amased, hearing the voice, but seeing no man. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=8}}† And Saul rose vp from the ground, and his eies being opened, he savv nothing. And they dravving him by the handes, brought him into Damascus. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=9}}† And he vvas three daies not seeing, and he did neither eate nor drinke.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=10}}† And there vvas a certaine disciple at Damascus, named Ananias: and our Lord said to him in a vision, Ananias. But he said, Loe, here I am Lord. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=11}}† And our Lord to him, Arise, & goe into the streate that is called Straight: and seeke in the house of Iudas, one named Saul of Tarsus. for behold he prayeth. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=12}}† ( And he savv a man named Ananias, comming in and imposing handes vpon him for to receiue his sight.) {{verse|chapter=9|verse=13}}† But Ananias ansvvered, Lord, I haue heard by many of this man, hovv much euil he hath done to thy sainctes in Hierusalem: {{verse|chapter=9|verse=14}}† and here he hath authoritie from the cheefe priests to binde al that inuocate thy name. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=15}}† And our Lord said to him, Goe, for a vessel of election is this man vnto me, to carie my name before the Gentiles, and kinges, and the children of Israël. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=16}}† For I vvil shevv him hovv great things he must suffer for my name.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=17}}† And Ananias vvent, and entred into the house: and imposing handes vpon him, he said, Brother Saul, our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}} hath sent me, he that appeared to thee in the vvay that thou camest: that thou maiest see and be filled vvith the holy Ghost. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=18}}† And forthvvith there fel from his eies as it<noinclude>{{rh||Rr ij|vvere}}</noinclude>
